text:
Marathon Petroleum stock surged 3.1% today and has climbed 8.2% over the past two weeks, driven by a tightening global oil supply picture. Crude oil prices have jumped sharply — U.S. oil is trading at $96/barrel while world oil tops $113/barrel, a gap that reflects geopolitical supply disruptions, particularly the escalating U.S.-Iran conflict and ongoing Middle East tensions that are threatening tanker traffic. Meanwhile, refineries are running at 92.5% capacity with gasoline and diesel inventories relatively lean, which means higher margins for refiners like MPC when crude inputs remain constrained but fuel demand stays firm.

The longer-term backdrop is also supportive: Saudi Aramco's warning that it could take two years to replenish global oil stockpiles signals that supply tightness will persist, and even though the G7 announced a release of 100 million barrels of diesel reserves, it's spread over four months and unlikely to quickly ease the current squeeze. For a refiner, tight crude and product supplies typically mean stronger profitability on the fuel they can produce and sell.
